problems.source_says: The paper gives these numbers only as students recruited per discipline (160, 496, 534; 1,190 in all). It never states how many were randomized. form-spec.md uses 'randomized' only for a count the paper gives at assignment ('Counts in prose') and bars inference (rule 1). The counts are also not distinct people. The paper removed 'duplications (ie students attending two subjects)' and says many Management students also took Marketing, so the 1,190 count some students twice. The form notes the Marketing-Management overlap under S2. The paper does not say which subject pairs the duplicates came from, so S1's 656 can also count twice a student who took both Entrepreneurship and Marketing. Fix: set n_randomized to null and keep 160, 496, and 534 in exclusions as recruited enrollments that include duplicates, or keep the values and label them recruited, not randomized. Criterion 2 does not depend on these counts.
problems.quote: Participants were recruited from three different first year academic disciplines, either elective or core to their degree and comprising 26 classes: Entrepreneurship (n = 160, 3 elective classes), Marketing (n = 496, 12 core classes)
problems.locator: PDF p. 7 (journal p. 1437), 'Description of participants and sampling' (recruited counts; duplicates sentence) and Methodology, third paragraph (Management students also in Marketing); form-spec.md, rule 1 and 'Counts in prose'

problems.form_value: '... outliers after non-normal residuals (number not stated) and two multivariate outliers by Mahalanobis distance (PDF p. 9).'
problems.source_says: The paper reports the two multivariate outliers once, in a pre-processing paragraph that covers 'both MANOVA analyses', and does not say which analysis they came from. The S1 entry assigns both to S1. The S2 entry says they belong to S2 'if they fell in this analysis'. The two entries disagree. Fix: give S1 the same caveat (two multivariate outliers removed, analysis not stated). No count changes.
problems.quote: Moreover, Mahalanobis distances revealed two multivariate outliers (χ²(4) = 18.46, p < .001), which were subsequently removed.

confirmed.statement: No page prints a count of people randomized, analyzed, or per arm. There is no flow diagram (no page after the cover holds an image), no supplement, and Tables 1-2 give cell means with unlabeled parentheticals and no n. The null n_analyzed values and the null arm counts are right.

confirmed.statement: The only printed counts are students recruited per discipline: Entrepreneurship n = 160 (3 elective classes), Marketing n = 496 (12 core classes), Management n = 534 (11 core classes), 26 classes and 1,190 students in all. They count students, not ideas, texts, ratings, sessions, or pairs. The Abstract and Methodology describe the trial as having 1,190 students.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7 (journal p. 1437), Methodology and 'Description of participants and sampling'; PDF p. 2, Abstract

confirmed.statement: Students were assigned one by one, within discipline, before their class. Five researchers collected the signed consent forms in class, so consent came after assignment.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7, 'Description of participants and sampling'; PDF p. 8 (journal p. 1438), 'Measures and procedures'

confirmed.statement: The removals between assignment and analysis match the form: duplicates (students attending two subjects), incomplete data, submissions of students who did not consent, univariate outliers after non-normal residuals (number not stated), and two multivariate outliers. Data collection in class implies that absent students were lost too, and the paper never counts them.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7 (duplicates); PDF p. 8, 'Measures and procedures' (incomplete data, non-consent); PDF p. 9, 'Data pre-processing' (outliers)

confirmed.statement: The error df fix the number of cases in each MANOVA. S1 is a full 2 x 2 between-subjects design with univariate F(1,198) and multivariate F(3, 196), so N = 198 + 4 = 202. S2 compares two groups with F(1,120) and F(3, 118), so N = 120 + 2 = 122. The printed partial eta-squared values (S1 interactions .04, .08, .019; S2 .14, .26, .33) and Pillai's traces (.06, .19, .09) reproduce from these df, so the df are not misprints. The form's 'about 202' and 'about 122' are exact case counts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 1439), Results and 'Entrepreneurship and marketing students'; PDF p. 10 (journal p. 1440), text below Table 2 and 'Management students'

confirmed.statement: The S2 originality test printed as F(1,198) is a misprint. Its partial eta-squared of .03 fits df 120 (3.50/123.50 = .028) and not df 198 (.017). The form flags the mismatch.

A case is a student on the natural reading. Fluency is a count of ideas 'by each respondent', each rater scored the submissions of all participating students, and outliers were screened per case. The paper never says how the three raters' scores were combined. If each case were one rater's record, S1 would still hold about 67 students (202/3), above 50, and S2 would hold about 41.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 8 (journal p. 1438), 'Measures and procedures'; PDF p. 9, 'Data pre-processing'

confirmed.statement: The S1 and S2 analysis samples share no students. The paper removed students who attended two subjects as duplicates, and it gave Management a different task because many Management students also took Marketing. The form records both facts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 7 (journal p. 1437), Methodology third paragraph and 'Description of participants and sampling'

confirmed.statement: Attrition is large and not reported by arm: 202 of 656 recruited (31 percent) reach the S1 analysis and 122 of 534 (23 percent) reach S2. Differential attrition cannot be checked, as the form says.

The per-arm estimates in open_questions reproduce if the parentheticals are standard errors from a pooled error term: Entrepreneurship about 38 per arm, Marketing about 71-78 control and 47-56 ChatGPT (about 126 in all), Management about 61-68 control and 54-61 ChatGPT. The form keeps them out of the count fields, as rule 1 requires.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 10, Tables 1-2; checker arithmetic with N = 202 and 122

confirmed.statement: No other paper reports these participants. No other candidate shares the authors or the trial (c921's Nguyen is an NTNU author, and c356 is a 33-student poem study), and a web search found no conference or preprint version. The empty sample_overlap stands.
confirmed.locator: candidates.json (author and title search); web search, 5 October 2026

confirmed.statement: The participants quotes for S1 and S2 are verbatim, and the participants locators (p. 7 recruitment; pp. 8-9 removals; p. 9 and p. 10 df) are right.
Criterion 2 holds on each study alone: 202 cases analyzed in S1 and 122 in S2, each randomized within discipline.

summary: The PDF supports the form's participant coding except for the randomized counts: S1's 656 and S2's 534 are the paper's recruited per-discipline enrollments, which it never gives as a count at assignment and which include students counted in two subjects, and the S1 exclusions assign the two multivariate outliers to S1 although the paper does not say which analysis they came from. Criterion 2 still holds, because the error df, which the printed effect sizes reproduce, fix 202 analyzed cases in S1 and 122 in S2, and S1 stays above 50 even if each case were one rater's record (about 67 students).
